correctness.rationale: Laurent--Nogueira Theorem 3(ii) supplies exact disjoint rational plateau endpoints. Their difference is the classical width \((1-\lambda)^2\lambda^{q-1}/(1-\lambda^q)\). The totient divisor identity proves exact normalization. Summatory totient with partial summation establishes the scaled density, Möbius inversion gives \(A_q(u)=u\varphi(q)+O(\tau(q))\) to prove joint angular equidistribution, and an exponential tail gives all integer moments. Independent exact checks verified 90 rational plateau widths, 1000 totient divisor identities and 90 midpoint itineraries. The verifier is supporting finite evidence, not the limit proof.

originality.rationale: The scientific claim is the joint scaled attracting-period and reduced-winding limit under uniform shift parameters and its exact moments; it does not claim the classical plateaux, their widths, or the classical divisor identity. Laurent--Nogueira and Nogueira--Pires full primary texts and the accessible Ding--Hemmer abstract describe dynamical mode locking and classifications, not the combined limit. Focused public-record searches found no equivalent theorem. The complete 1987 and 1999 historical texts remain inaccessible, so possible earlier implication remains an explicitly unresolved priority risk, not a claimed proof of unique priority.
residual_risks: The complete Ding--Hemmer 1987 article was not accessible; its possible pre-existing distributional consequences cannot be definitively excluded.
The complete Bugeaud--Conze 1999 article was not accessible; an unindexed earlier scaling theorem is possible.

value.rationale: The least period and rational winding fraction are intrinsic dynamical observables of a fully specified natural family. The loss-of-contraction window contains all denominator scales \(q\asymp (1-\lambda)^{-1}\); rather than yielding a deterministic typical period, it has a universal nontrivial density, explicit zeta moments, and asymptotic independence from the winding fraction. This quantifies an overlooked statistical phase transition of classic mode locking, beyond a textbook algebraic identity.
